title: Power Pages: security agent in design studio configures authentication and authorisation
summary: Hold: the briefing understates the documented Copilot hub controls for maker AI features by treating their applicability as wholly unconfirmed. The core feature description, approval requirement, roadmap dates and listed control paths are supported, but automatic configuration of redirect settings is not established by the sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing model specific to the design studio security agent.

claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "licensing". Read the roadmap record, security-agent and faq-security-agent in full; none states a separate licence.

claims.claim: The roadmap and preview feature documentation state no feature-specific meter or credit charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent licensing credits pricing; "Power Pages" "security agent" "licensing". Read security-agent, faq-security-agent and assign-licensing; searched the licensing FAQ for security agent, Copilot and credit. No feature-specific meter found.

claims.claim: General-availability pricing and a consumption model specific to this agent are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent licensing credits pricing; "Power Pages" "security agent" "licensing". Opened security-agent, faq-security-agent, assign-licensing and the licensing FAQ; no GA security-agent price or consumption model found.

claims.claim: The cited Power Pages licensing page covers subscriptions for the underlying site.
claims.quote: As you work on projects and need to establish permanent sites that don't expire, you can apply Power Pages subscriptions and convert websites from trial to production.

claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... In the Manage pane, select Tenant settings. ... Publish Copilots with AI features

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the Publish Copilots with AI features tenant setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Publish Copilots with AI features" "PowerShell" "API"; "Publish" "AI" "Set-TenantSettings". Read tenant-settings and Set-TenantSettings search excerpts; no setting-specific request property or call found.

claims.quote: To view or update these settings, navigate to Copilot hub > Power Pages > Settings in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the per-environment Copilot hub Power Pages AI settings is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "Copilot" "settings" "API" "PowerShell"; "Copilot hub" "Power Pages" "settings" "REST"; Power Pages Copilot environment pac settings; Power Pages AI organization Web API settings. Read copilot-hub and admin-api excerpts; no equivalent call found.

claims.claim: The design studio provides the site scan under Security workspace > Run scan.
claims.quote: After you receive the email confirmation, you can view the scan report summary by returning to the Run scan section of the Security workspace.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and controls[3].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: No switch specific to the security-agent chat assistant is documented on the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "security agent" "Power Pages" "disable"; "Power Pages" "security agent" "disable" "API". Opened security-agent, faq-security-agent and copilot-hub; read admin-api results. Found general maker AI controls, but no separate chat-assistant switch.

claims.claim: The feature documentation does not specify roles or privileges required to use the agent.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "roles". Read security-agent and faq-security-agent in full and opened use-security-workspace; none states security-agent access roles or privileges.

claims.claim: The publishing tenant control is documented as relevant to the site chatbot.
claims.quote: Chat agent (site Copilot) specific setting: If the setting for “Publish bots with AI” is disabled at the tenant level, admins are unable to configure site Copilot at the environment level.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the site-chatbot publishing tenant setting applies to the security-agent chat assistant.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Publish Copilots with AI features tenant settings PowerShell API publish bots AI; Power Pages security agent disable. Read tenant-settings, copilot-hub and security-agent; no connection from this publishing setting to the security assistant found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and first prose paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated which Copilot governance settings apply to the agent, so Copilot hub maker AI governance is treated as unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Enable or disable AI features for makers Control whether makers in specific environments can use AI features. ... Admins manage AI-powered experiences for makers and site users through the Copilot hub
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].note and the matching table note with: 'Copilot hub controls whether makers in specific environments can use AI features; a separate Security agent switch is not documented.' Replace the first two sentences after the table with: 'The security agent is an AI-powered maker tool. Copilot hub documents controls to enable or disable AI features for makers in specific environments; Microsoft does not name a separate Security agent switch.' Retain the qualification on controls[0], which concerns site-chatbot publishing rather than maker AI governance.

claims.claim: Copilot hub manages governance settings for Copilot features in Power Pages.
claims.quote: Going forward, all governance settings for Copilot features must be managed through the Copilot hub.

claims.claim: The older tenant-level governance configuration is deprecated.
claims.quote: The tenant-level governance configuration feature is now deprecated. While your existing settings will remain in place, we strongly recommend reviewing and validating them

claims.claim: The older control governed AI experiences for website users and explicitly excluded maker experiences.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can choose to disable Generative AI features for your website users. ... The following AI-powered experiences are governed separately and are not covered by this control: ... Maker experiences

claims.claim: Security agent is an AI assistant embedded in the Power Pages design studio Security workspace.
claims.quote: Security agent is an AI-powered assistant built into the Power Pages Security workspace that helps makers review, configure, and strengthen the security of their Power Pages sites by using natural language.

claims.claim: Makers open the Security agent tab and use its chat panel for natural-language risk review, configuration explanations and guided actions.
claims.quote: Makers can open the security agent tab to access the embedded chat panel and security tools. From there, they can interact using natural language to review risks, understand configurations, and take guided actions.

claims.claim: Site security posture review is one of the preview agent's four primary scenarios.
claims.quote: Security agent supports four primary security scenarios that cover the core areas of Power Pages site protection. ... Site security posture review

claims.claim: The agent helps create and update web roles.
claims.quote: The agent helps create and update web roles, page permissions, and table permissions.

claims.claim: The agent helps create and update page permissions.
claims.quote: The agent helps create and update web roles, page permissions, and table permissions.

claims.claim: The agent helps create and update table permissions.
claims.quote: The agent helps create and update web roles, page permissions, and table permissions.

claims.claim: Authentication configuration and troubleshooting supports Microsoft Entra ID, OpenID Connect and SAML 2.0.
claims.quote: The agent supports Microsoft Entra ID, OpenID Connect, and SAML 2.0, and recommends configuration updates to resolve authentication problems.

claims.claim: Application-security configuration covers Content Security Policy, HTTP security headers, CORS, cookies and session management.
claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including Content Security Policy (CSP), HTTP security headers, CORS, cookie settings, session management, and WAF-related configurations.

claims.claim: Recommendations draw on the site's configuration, data schema and permissions.
claims.quote: For authorization, the security agent helps configure web roles and data access permissions. Using the site’s data schema and usage patterns, it suggests appropriate access levels

claims.claim: The agent can configure identity providers.
claims.quote: Configure authentication providers, validate authentication settings, and diagnose common sign-in problems.

claims.claim: The agent can configure redirect settings.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "redirect". Opened security-agent and read the roadmap description. The roadmap mentions recommendations for validating redirect settings, not execution of redirect-setting changes; Learn does not state that capability.
claims.fix: Remove 'redirect settings and' from the bullet, leaving: 'The agent can configure identity providers and session controls.'

claims.claim: The agent can configure session controls.
claims.quote: Review and configure application-level security settings including ... session management ... Update the session timeout for inactive users.

claims.claim: The agent recommends least-privilege access, without guaranteeing that recommendations are correct.
claims.quote: It explains existing authorization settings and recommends least-privilege access based on your site's configuration. ... Review all proposed configuration changes before approving write actions.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent requests approval before applying any configuration change.
claims.quote: For any configuration changes, the agent always requests your approval before making updates, so you remain in control of your site's security.

claims.claim: After applying an approved change, the agent confirms exactly what was updated.
claims.quote: Before applying any change, it requests your approval and, once complete, confirms exactly what was updated.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support

claims.quote: Security agent overview (preview) ... [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] ... This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The preview is not meant for production use.
claims.quote: Preview features aren’t meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Use Security agent in development or test environments before promoting changes to production.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The documented best practices call for reviewing writes and deploying approved changes through the organisation's standard ALM process.
claims.quote: Review all proposed configuration changes before approving write actions. ... Validate and deploy approved changes using your organization's standard ALM process.

claims.claim: Power Pages sites serve public-facing or external-access scenarios.
claims.quote: The Power Pages website security agent is an AI-assisted system integrated into Microsoft Power Pages design studio that helps makers proactively secure their public-facing websites.

claims.claim: Overly permissive table permissions can expose data, including to anonymous users.
claims.quote: Check whether sensitive Dataverse tables are exposed through overly permissive permissions. ... Remove anonymous access from this table permission.

claims.claim: The agent is intended to lower the security expertise needed by makers to configure access.

claims.claim: The FAQ describes a wider security-agent system that includes scheduled vulnerability scanning.
claims.quote: It combines scheduled vulnerability scanning, real-time traffic anomaly detection, and guided remediation to assist non-security-expert makers in maintaining a secure posture.

claims.claim: The chat assistant's posture review analyses vulnerability scan findings.
claims.quote: The agent analyzes authentication settings, authorization configuration, security settings, vulnerability scan findings, and site configuration

claims.claim: A chat command that starts a security scan is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "security agent" "start" "scan" "chat". Read security-agent, faq-security-agent, security-scan and use-security-workspace. Chat prompts review or summarise scan findings; scan execution is documented separately, not as a chat command.

claims.claim: Administrators can initiate scans from the Power Platform admin center's website security pages.
claims.quote: Site-specific details, including the scan status, scan score (number of passed/failed checks), if the scan is completed, a view of the scan results, and an option to initiate the scan.

claims.where: Scope; Governance controls prose; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The chat assistant targets site makers and owners configuring sites, rather than site visitors.
claims.quote: Security agent is an AI-powered assistant built into the Power Pages Security workspace that helps makers review, configure, and strengthen the security of their Power Pages sites

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the page's automatic enablement, medium risk and November 2026 target.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; defaultState: "on"; risk: "medium"; targetDate: "November CY2026"; "Service owners should decide whether AI-assisted security configuration is acceptable under their change process"
claims.fix: Change action from 'prepare' to 'act-now': on the 2026-11-16 run date, the stated automatic enablement, medium risk and November target satisfy the standard's near-term decision criterion.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table

claims.quote: Review web roles and table permissions after agent-driven changes. ... Controls: Publish Copilots with AI features; AI features for Power Pages per environment; Security scan of a site; Switch specific to the security agent.
claims.fix: The After rollout step 'Review web roles and table permissions after agent-driven changes' has no corresponding web-role or table-permission control row.
